Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

dramatic adjective

of the theatre

also theatrical, dramatic art, stage (adjective)

classical

Cic. Fam. 7.1.4: lūdīs scaenicīs
Varr. LL 9.17: poētae scaenicī (Lewis & Short)

scaenicus, scaenica, scaenicum

of the stage, theatrical

lūdī scaenicī, plays, as against the games of the circus; poēta scaenicus, a dramatist; as a noun scaenicus is an actor (Cic. Off. 1.114).

Other words

  • theātrālis, theātrāle — of the theatre

    also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 115: theātrālēs gladiātōriīque cōnsessūs (Lewis & Short)

    Of the theatre and its audience rather than of plays; Quintilian’s theātrālis hūmānitās is put on for show (Quint. 2.2.10).

  • drāmaticus, drāmatica, drāmaticum — dramatic (of poetry in dialogue)

    also used · late Latin · Diom. p. 480 P.: drāmaticum poēma (Lewis & Short, s.v. drāma)

    A grammarian’s term for poetry in which the characters speak.

Examples

  • hīs ego tamen diēbus lūdīs scaenicīs … dīrūpī mē paene in jūdiciō

    yet these days, during the plays, I nearly burst myself in a trialCic. Fam. 7.1.4

  • nē scaenicī plūs quam nōs videantur habēre prūdentiae

    so that actors may not seem to have more sense than we haveCic. Off. 1.114

See also play, theatre, actor, stage.
